question: A cylinder whose height is eight times its radius is melted and cast into spherical balls each of half the radius of the cylinder. Find the number of spherical balls.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume is conserved ⇒ Number of spheres = Volume of cylinder ÷ Volume of one sphere

Cylinder: h = 8r ⇒ Volume = πr² × 8r = 8πr³

Sphere: radius = r/2 ⇒ Volume = (4/3)π(r/2)³ = (1/6)πr³

Number = 8πr³ ÷ (1/6)πr³ = 8 × 6 = 48

**∴ Answer = 48**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cylinder radius = r, height = 8r; Sphere radius = r/2

**Formula used:**

Volume of cylinder = πr²h; Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³

 
• 
• r 8r r/2 

Cylinder volume = πr² × 8r = 8πr³

Sphere volume = (4/3)π(r/2)³ = (1/6)πr³

**Calculation:**

⇒ Number of spheres = Total volume ÷ Volume of one sphere

⇒ = 8πr³ ÷ (1/6)πr³

⇒ = 8 × 6

⇒ = 48

**∴ The correct answer is 48.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Conservation

When a solid is melted and recast, total volume remains constant.

Cylinder Volume

Volume = πr²h

Sphere Volume

Volume = (4/3)πr³

Scaling Rule

If radius changes by factor k, volume changes by k³.
